en: The Apadāna of the Elder Sappidāyaka Hatthivagga 9 [Verse 1] When the Buddha Kassapa was present in the world, I was a wealthy householder, possessing great riches and abundant wealth. [Verse 2] I gave a gift of ghee to the Teacher, the Great Sage, who was surrounded by a multitude of monks, while he was seated upon a seat. [Verse 3] Because of that gift of ghee, I have attained the fruit of Stream-entry; having abandoned birth and death, I have reached the end of suffering. [Verse 4] For eighty-four thousand aeons I dwelt in heaven; for eighty-four thousand aeons I lived as a human being. [Verse 5] In this final existence, I have become a monk; having abandoned birth and death, I have reached the end of suffering. [Verse 6] I am now a stream-enterer, no longer subject to rebirth in the lower realms; having attained the certainty of enlightenment, I am destined for supreme peace. [Verse 7] I have seen the Tathāgata, the one with vision, the Great Sage; I have heard his Dhamma, which leads to the cessation of suffering. [Verse 8] Having heard the Dhamma, I have practiced it; having practiced it, I have realized its fruit. I am now a stream-enterer, no longer subject to rebirth in the lower realms. “Seated in his magnificent palace,
surrounded by a host of women,
he saw a sick ascetic.”
I entered the house together with him.
There sat the Great Hero,
the God of Gods, the Bull among Men.
Ghee and oil were given by me to the Great Sage Siddhattha,
having seen his distress calmed.
With serene faculties and a bright face,
having bowed at the Teacher’s feet,
I praised him in the past.
Seeing my state of profound confidence,
the wise one, who had reached the perfection of psychic power, soared up into the sky.
Like king swans in the sky,
ninety-four eons ago,
I gave that gift at that time.
I do not recall ever being born in an evil state;
this is the fruit of ghee and sesame oil.
Seventeen aeons from now,
Named Jutideva,
he was a wheel-turning monarch of great power, endowed with the seven treasures.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable Elder Sappidāyaka spoke these verses.
The legend of the Elder Sappidāyaka is the ninth.
